By way of this criminal misc. petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the accused-petitioners have approached this Court with a prayer to quash the FIR No. 27/2022 registered at Police Station Mahila Thana, District Ajmer for the [2024:RJ-JP:23363] (2 of 3)

1 [CRLMP-1820/2022] offences punishable under Sections 498A and 406 of IPC alongwith all consequential and subsequent proceedings arising thereto.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that parties have resolved their dispute amicably and entered into a compromise.

Counsel further submits that an application under Section 13B of Hindu Marriage Act has been filed by petitioner and complainant- respondent no.2 before the Family Court for grant of divorce by mutual consent.
He submits that compromise deed is annexed with this petition.
3. Complainant-respondent No. 2 is present in person and duly identified by her counsel.
Learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant do not dispute the aforesaid factual position.

Under the instructions of the complainant, her counsel submits that parties have resolved their dispute amicably and complainant has no objection if the FIR in question and all subsequent proceedings are quashed.

4. In view of the aforesaid and considering the submissions made on behalf of the respective parties;
the material made available for my perusal; considering that the petitioner No.1 and the complainant-respondent No.2 (husband and wife respectively) have resolved their dispute, this Court is of the view that in order to establish peace and harmony between the petitioner and complainant and in order to let them live peacefully in the future life, and also finding that the present case is wholly covered by the principle of law laid down by Hon'ble the Supreme Court in the case of Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab & Anr reported in 2012 Cr.L.J. (SC) 4934 and in the case of State of Haryana & [2024:RJ-JP:23363] (3 of 3) [CRLMP-1820/2022] Ors. Vs. Choudhary Bhajan Lal & Ors. [AIR 1992 SC 604]
